title: Sebastian and the Sigil
premise: Jude Underhill, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead, has spent years hiding his gift while keeping ledgers for the Meridian Guild, a trade house dealing in impossible things. When a dying courier presses a sigil-marked map into his hands, Jude learns the covenant binding the living realm to the Hollow is failing, and that he himself carries the blood of the last covenant-keepers. Hunted by guild enforcers who want the map silenced, Jude gathers an unlikely found family—a disgraced sigilwright, a Hollow-born child, and a ghost who refuses to move on—to reforge the covenant at the Threshold Spire. In the end, Jude must choose between erasing his painful gift forever or becoming the living seal between realms; he chooses to stay, imperfect and heard at last, and the covenant holds.
about_author: Isandro Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funerary carvings in coastal graveyards before turning to fiction. They write quiet, haunted fantasies about people who belong to no one until they find each other.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. We meet him carving a memorial bone token while the dead murmur around him, then closing the guild's night ledgers. He catalogs an impossible item—a key that unlocks memories—and hides his gift from his supervisor. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence; Jude believes invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Loading Dock
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A bleeding courier stumbles into the guild yard at closing bell, presses a wax-sealed map into Jude's hands, and dies whispering 'the Spire remembers.' The dead woman's voice lingers only for Jude. Emotional beat: terror of being seen; the first crack in his careful anonymity.

chapters.title: What the Dead Woman Knew
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Interrogated by guild enforcer Captain Vess, Jude lies badly about the map. Alone, he unrolls it: a sigil matching the birthmark scar on his own wrist. The dead courier's ghost begins following him. Emotional beat: dread curdling into reluctant curiosity—he cannot unknow what he is.

chapters.title: The Sigilwright Who Fell
chapters.summary: Jude seeks out Maren Oduya, a disgraced sigilwright drunk in a canal-side tenement, because her name appears in the ledger beside the word 'covenant.' She recognizes the mark instantly and sobers fast. Emotional beat: two exiles recognizing each other's damage; the first fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Vess Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Guild enforcers raid Maren's workshop; she and Jude escape through the bone-carvers' tunnels beneath the city. Vess reveals the guild has been suppressing covenant knowledge for decades—and that Jude's parents were keepers. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution Jude served; flight into the unknown.

chapters.title: The Child from the Hollow
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Hiding in the marshes, they find Pip, a feral Hollow-born child who slipped through a failing veil and cannot get home. Pip can see Jude's ghosts plainly and isn't afraid of them. Emotional beat: unexpected tenderness; Jude's protective instincts override his self-preservation.

chapters.title: Three Names in an Old Book
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. In a smuggler's archive, they learn the covenant requires three keeper-bloods to renew it at the Threshold Spire before the autumn equinox—eleven days away. The third bloodline is thought extinct. The ghost courier finally speaks her name: Odile, a former keeper. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Odile's Long Walk
chapters.summary: Odile's POV (rendered through Jude hearing her). Her ghost recounts her death guarding the map and her guilt over abandoning her fellow keepers. She teaches Jude to listen deliberately instead of drowning in the dead's noise. Emotional beat: grief transformed into mentorship; Jude's gift becomes a skill, not a curse.

chapters.title: The Guild's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Vess corners Jude alone—not to arrest him, but to offer restoration of his old life if he surrenders the map. She claims the covenant's fall would free the guild to trade across realms unchecked. Emotional beat: temptation of belonging-by-return versus belonging-by-choice; Jude refuses, shaking.

chapters.title: Pip's Doorway
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip leads them to a thin place where the veil is tearing, showing them the Hollow's slow unraveling—fading villages, dissolving dead. Pip begs to go home. Jude realizes the covenant's failure is already killing a world. Emotional beat: stakes made flesh; abstract duty becomes love for one small child.

chapters.title: Blood in the Bone Market
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Seeking the third bloodline, they infiltrate the bone market where Jude's carving skills earn passage. They discover a keeper descendant sold as a living relic: Sef, a mute old man displayed in a collector's case. Emotional beat: righteous anger; Jude chooses open defiance over stealth for the first time.

chapters.title: The Rescue That Wasn't Stealthy
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. A chaotic rescue frees Sef but burns their cover completely; Vess now knows their route to the Spire. Sef, voiceless, communicates through carved bone tokens—the same craft as Jude. Emotional beat: camaraderie forged in disaster; the group stops being allies and becomes family.

chapters.title: What Jude Buried
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Around a fire, Jude finally tells the truth: he heard his mother die as a boy and ran rather than answer her voice, and has muted his gift ever since. Odile forgives him; Pip falls asleep against his shoulder. Emotional beat: confession and absolution; the wound that shaped him finally aired.

chapters.title: Vess's True Master
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess reports to Guildmaster Corvane, revealed as the original betrayer of the covenant, who plans to let the Hollow die and harvest its magic. Vess wavers—she was told she was protecting the city. Emotional beat: antagonist humanized; doubt planted in the enemy camp.

chapters.title: The Ascent Begins
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Four days remain. The company climbs toward the Threshold Spire through the Gray Pass, pursued by guild hunters. An avalanche separates them; Jude must trust Maren and Sef to survive without him. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into trust; leadership he never asked for.

chapters.title: The Spire Remembers
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Inside the Spire, the walls hold the memories of every keeper who ever renewed the covenant—including Jude's parents, alive in stone. Jude meets their echo and receives the rite's final requirement: a keeper must give up what they most hide. Emotional beat: awe and heartbreak; the past offering a hand forward.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Gate
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Corvane's forces storm the Spire; Vess, ordered to kill the keepers, instead turns on Corvane and buys them time, falling wounded. Sef sacrifices himself to complete the first seal, pressing his carved tokens into Jude's hands. Emotional beat: sacrifice stacking on sacrifice; the cost made real.

chapters.title: The Rite of Three
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Maren inscribes the great sigil, Odile lends her keeper's death-memory, and Jude offers the thing he most hid: his silence, his muting of the dead. The covenant demands he hear everything, forever, without flinching. Emotional beat: climax of identity; Jude accepts his whole self as the price and the gift.

chapters.title: Where the Veil Mends
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The covenant reforges; the veil knits closed—but leaves one door open, sized for a child. Pip walks through to the Hollow, promising to return when the door swings both ways again. Emotional beat: bittersweet release; loving someone means letting them go home.

chapters.title: Ledgers, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Aftermath in the city: Corvane arrested by his own guild, Vess recovering and quietly reassigned, the Meridian Guild restructured under new honest management—with Maren asked to oversee its impossible-things registry. Emotional beat: institutions can change when individuals refuse to look away.

chapters.title: The Carver Who Is Heard
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude opens a small workshop above the guild hall, carving memorials and listening willingly to the dead who need witnessing. Odile, her purpose fulfilled, fades with a smile. He is no longer invisible; clients seek him out by name. Emotional beat: quiet joy; identity fully claimed.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Sigil
chapters.summary: Epilogue, mostly Pip's POV framed as a story Pip tells Hollow children. Years later, the two-way door opens and Pip returns, taller, carrying a carved bone token shaped like a spire. Jude, surrounded by his strange family, adds a new page to the ledger. Emotional beat: belonging completed; the found family endures, and the story becomes legend.
